summary.intent: Execute Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) using the GSD wave-based orchestration system, then review the code, create a PR, and ensure test/build coverage is solid.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 completed with all 2 plans across 2 waves merged, verified, and pushed as PR FSM1/cipher-box#416. Code was cleaned up, SDK integration tests and E2E batch upload tests were added, the encrypt worker was added to tsconfig type-checking, and two lint warnings were fixed.

repo: Worker files must be added to `apps/web/tsconfig.sw.json` to be type-checked in CI — the main tsconfig.json excludes them but doesn't include them in any tsconfig by default. The existing pattern is `decrypt-sw.ts` in tsconfig.sw.json.
The existing `@cipherbox/crypto` package uses Web Crypto API only (no Node.js crypto), making it safe to use directly inside Web Workers without any additional configuration.
Vite handles `new Worker(new URL(..., import.meta.url))` natively — no vite.config changes needed for workers.
FolderMetadata type (in packages/core/src/folder/types.ts) requires `version` and `children` fields at minimum.
The codebase uses a structured logger rather than `console.warn/log/error` — raw console calls are a code smell here.
apps/web/CLAUDE.md has guidance against using Blob `.buffer` — pre-existing violation in upload.service.ts.
Task-reference comments like `(D-01)`, `(D-03)` are considered noise and should be removed or replaced with actual WHY context.
p-limit is used for concurrency control in the SDK batch upload pipeline with a pool of 3 concurrent uploads.

code.finding: The encryption result type was defined inline 4 times; should use ReturnType<ExternalEncryptFn> / Parameters<ExternalEncryptFn> from @cipherbox/sdk-core for a single source of truth.
useDropUpload now calls client.uploadFiles() batch method instead of the previous sequential upload loop.
destroyEncryptionWorker() is called here on logout for proper cleanup.
Mock of loadFolderMetadata return value originally typed as `any` — should use the FolderMetadata shape with `version` and `children` fields.
Pre-existing `any` type in test mock — not Phase 37 code but flagged by lint:fix run.

workflow: GSD verifier agents can produce false negatives when run immediately after cherry-picking commits — the filesystem may not reflect the new git state yet. Always spot-check key artifact existence directly after verification reports gaps_found.

Worktree branch refs don't always update automatically after agent commits — the worktree HEAD may have commits that the named branch ref doesn't point to. Requires manual cherry-pick or explicit branch reset.
When GSD executor agents run in worktree isolation with --no-verify, merging back requires care: stash local changes, merge worktree branch, resolve conflicts (e.g. STATE.md), restore stash.

The `classifyHandoffIfNeeded` Claude Code runtime bug can cause agents to report failure even when all work is complete — spot-checking SUMMARY.md existence and git log is the reliable completion signal.
Treating lint warnings as errors in tests requires explicit discipline — `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` warnings in test files are easy to miss and should be treated as blockers.

friction: Wave 2 worktree branch ref was not updated after agent commits — the branch pointed to an old commit while the actual HEAD had all the work. Required undoing a bad merge and cherry-picking 3 commits manually.

The GSD verifier produced false negatives for all 4 Wave 2 artifacts (encrypt.worker.ts, encrypt-worker.service.ts, useDropUpload rewire, destroyEncryptionWorker) because it ran before cherry-picked commits were visible. Required manually editing VERIFICATION.md to correct the status.
Phase completion (gsd-tools phase complete) and PROJECT.md update had to be re-run after fixing the branch state, since the first run happened on the wrong branch.
A stale worktree (`cipher-box-worktree-parallel` on `docs/worktree-e2e-env-learnings`) was left from a prior session and needed manual cleanup.
The orchestrator temporarily navigated into a worktree directory instead of the main repo, causing a branch confusion that required investigation.
open_items: Web E2E tests not updated for multi-file batch upload flows — existing tests only cover serial single-file uploads. Needs browser-level drag-drop test with real app running.

Upfront file buffer allocation in uploadFiles() — all files are read into Uint8Array before upload starts, which is memory-inefficient for large batches. Fixing requires changing SDK contract to accept File objects instead of Uint8Array. Bounded by MAX_FILE_SIZE (100MB) for now.
Pre-existing Blob `.buffer` usage in apps/web/src/services/upload.service.ts violates apps/web/CLAUDE.md guidance — should be fixed separately.
uploadFiles() has no integration tests against a real server in the sdk-e2e suite's file-operations.test.ts (the main integration suite) — only a new standalone batch-upload.test.ts was added.
